# Status report: jf2 allocator test on kestrel (2026-11-20)

## Short version

On a read-heavy workload (95% reads), jf2 (our fork of the jemalloc memory allocator) reduced the p99 latency (the latency that 99% of requests finish within) of kestrel (our key-value store) from 2140 us to 870 us, a 59.3% reduction. Throughput and median latency did not change beyond the run-to-run range. Two items are not resolved: jf2 used 5.7 GB (9.3%) more memory, which needs approval from the capacity team, and the write-heavy workload has not been tested.

## Words used here

- **kestrel**: our key-value store, the program under test.
- **jemalloc**: the memory allocator library that kestrel uses today, version 5.3.
- **jf2**: our fork of jemalloc.
- **Build A**: main@4f1c2aa with jemalloc 5.3.
- **Build B**: the same commit with jf2.
- **YCSB-B**: workload B of the Yahoo Cloud Serving Benchmark, 95% reads and 5% updates.
- **YCSB-A**: workload A of the same benchmark, 50% reads and 50% updates (write-heavy).
- **p50, p99, p99.9**: latency percentiles. 99% of requests finish at or below the p99 value. p50 is the median.
- **us**: microseconds.
- **kops/s**: thousand operations per second.
- **RSS**: resident set size, the physical memory that the process holds.
- **Latency spike**: a short period in which latency is much higher than normal.
- **Decay purge**: the jemalloc step that returns unused memory pages to the operating system after a delay.
- **perf**: the Linux sampling profiler.
- **je_arena_decay**: the jemalloc function that perf reported during the spikes.
- **Load average**: the average number of tasks that are running or waiting for a CPU.
- **NUMA pinning**: binding a process to the CPUs and memory of one processor socket.
- **Staging**: the pre-production environment.

## Setup

- **Host:** bench-07 (2 x 32-core Xeon, 512 GB RAM), kernel 6.8.
- **System load:** the load average was 0.4 before the runs. The host has 64 cores, so it was idle.
- **Builds:** A and B come from the same commit. Only the allocator differs.
- **Workload:** YCSB-B, 64 client threads, 10 minutes per run.
- **Runs:** 5 per build, in alternating order (A, B, A, B, ...).

## Results

Median of 5 runs. One block = 200 us. Shorter is better.

```
p99    A  ███████████  2140 us
       B  ████  870 us                (-59.3%)
p99.9  A  █████████████████████████████████████████████████  9800 us
       B  ████████████████  3100 us   (-68.4%)
```

Only the high percentiles moved. Throughput and p50 stayed the same.

| Metric, median (min..max) | A (jemalloc 5.3) | B (jf2) | Change B vs A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput, kops/s | 412 (405..418) | 409 (401..415) | -3 (-0.7%), ranges overlap |
| p50 latency, us | 118 (116..121) | 119 (117..121) | +1 (+0.8%), ranges overlap |
| p99 latency, us | 2140 (1890..2610) | 870 (820..940) | -1270 (-59.3%), no overlap |
| p99.9 latency, us | 9800 (7200..14100) | 3100 (2700..3900) | -6700 (-68.4%), no overlap |
| RSS at end of run, GB | 61.2 | 66.9 | +5.7 (+9.3%), range not recorded |

What the data shows:

- **p99 latency is lower with jf2 in every run.** The highest B run was 940 us. The lowest A run was 1890 us.
- **p99.9 latency is lower with jf2 in every run.** The highest B run was 3900 us. The lowest A run was 7200 us.
- **Throughput did not change measurably.** The medians differ by 3 kops/s. The range inside each build is larger (13 kops/s for A, 14 kops/s for B).
- **p50 latency did not change measurably.** The medians differ by 1 us. The ranges are 116..121 us for A and 117..121 us for B.
- **jf2 uses more memory.** RSS at the end of the run was 5.7 GB higher, which is about 1.1% of the 512 GB on bench-07.
- **Insufficient data: run-to-run range of RSS.** The notes give one RSS value per build. The per-run RSS values would resolve this.

## Cause of the spikes in build A

- **Timing:** the spikes in A occurred at the same times as the jemalloc decay purge.
- **Profile:** perf attributed 31% of the samples inside the spike windows to je_arena_decay.
- **Build B:** jf2 does the purge in a background thread.
- **Insufficient data:** the notes do not record the je_arena_decay share outside the spike windows. That number would show how specific the 31% is to the spikes.

## One run was replaced

- Run 3 of build B had a 40 s pause at minute 7.
- The pause was traced to logrotate (the log rotation tool), started by the nightly cron job (the system task scheduler). The allocator was not involved.
- The run was repeated. The results above use the repeated run.

## Not tested

- YCSB-A (write-heavy).
- More than 64 client threads.
- NUMA pinning.

The results above apply only to YCSB-B at 64 client threads without NUMA pinning.

## Decision needed

- Is an RSS increase of 5.7 GB (9.3%) acceptable? The capacity team must approve it.

## Next steps

1. Run YCSB-A on 2026-11-21.
2. Ask the capacity team about the RSS increase.
3. If the capacity team approves, enable jf2 in staging through a feature flag (a configuration switch that is off by default).

Source for all numbers: raw test notes from 2026-11-20 on bench-07.

---

Note on the date: I converted "tomorrow" in your notes to 2026-11-21, which is a Saturday. Change it if you meant Monday, 2026-11-23.
